whatItIs.text: The seed of an aquatic grass and the staple food of over half the world; long-grain types stay fluffy, short-grain types go sticky, and that difference is written in the grain's starch.

historyNote.text: Asian rice was domesticated in China some 13,500-8,200 years ago; African rice was domesticated independently in West Africa about 3,000 years ago. Black rice earned the name 'forbidden rice' because it was reserved for royalty in ancient China.

howToChoose.text: Match the grain to the dish: basmati or long-grain for pilafs, jasmine for fragrance, short-grain or sushi rice for sticking, arborio for risotto; brown rice for fibre if the cooking time allows.

storage.text: Keep dry in a sealed container in a cool cupboard; cooked rice is the exception and goes straight to the fridge.

useItUp.text: Day-old rice is the best fried rice — drier grains stay separate; it also thickens soups and becomes rice pudding with milk and sugar.

substitutions.note: similar fluffy role, nuttier and protein-richer; cooks faster
